meta.title: Official-source re-checks performed on 2026-11-02
meta.method: Each URL was opened with a page-retrieval tool on 2026-11-02 and the returned text was read. 'excerpt' quotes what the page actually returned. A page that does not return the value it is cited for is recorded as NOT CONFIRMED, not as confirmed.
meta.policy: Nothing here is inferred. Where a page could not be read, the entry says so and the dependent site claim is flagged.

checks.label: nflverse data dictionary - Schedules (nflreadr)
checks.supports: Field definitions behind the data QA: result, total, rest days, moneylines.
checks.excerpt: 'result ... The number of points the home team scored minus the number of points the visiting team scored. Equals h_score - v_score.' / 'total ... The sum of each team's score in the game.' / 'away_rest ... Days of rest that the away team is coming off of.'
checks.note: The visible portion of the dictionary defines result, total, rest and moneyline fields, but not spread_line (entries 26-45 were not returned). The site's ATS sign convention is therefore proven empirically from the data (see the sign-convention checks), not from this page - the citation is accurate for the field definitions it is attached to on the data-integrity table, and weaker than it looks where it is attached to the sign-convention table.

asset_provenance.method: Each of the 31 assets recorded in data/derived/manifest.json was looked up by name in the live GitHub release metadata on 2026-11-02 and its current byte size compared with the size recorded at build time.
asset_provenance.verdict: The historical seasons are byte-identical to what the build recorded, so the model's training data is intact. The three current-season assets have been updated upstream, which is exactly why a rebuild of the committed extract stops at gameday 2026-10-29 while NFL.com already lists the completed Week 8.
